questions.q: What is the scuttlebutt method Fisher recommends?
a: Contacting stakeholders directly to learn about a company firsthand
Studying a company's published annual reports in detail
Following analysts' ratings on financial news sites
Testing a company's products as an ordinary customer
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes scuttlebutt as reaching out to people connected to the company to form an accurate, personal view.

questions.q: What should a long-term investor do when a stock's price falls?
a: Buy, if the company's fundamentals are still sound
Sell quickly to avoid even bigger losses
Wait until the price returns to its old high
Move everything into bonds until the market settles
questions.why: Lesson 2 says dips are usually temporary and that a sound company's falling price is the moment to buy.

questions.q: How does the summary describe the stock market in the short term?
a: Irrational and driven by short-term events
Efficient and always correctly priced
Predictable and easy to time
Calm and largely unaffected by news
questions.why: The summary says the market acts irrationally on short-term news, which creates overvalued and undervalued stocks.

questions.q: Which qualities does Fisher look for in a mature company?
a: Strong margins, loyal customers and patents or scale
Fast growth, heavy borrowing and cheap labor
New leadership, low prices and high volume
Celebrity endorsements and constant rebranding
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists high margins, employee satisfaction, customer retention, patents and distribution as signs of a strong future.

questions.q: What mistake does the summary say average investors keep making?
a: Panic selling when prices drop, then buying after they recover
Holding a stock through every market dip
Researching companies thoroughly before investing
Spreading their money across many industries
questions.why: The summary describes investors who sell in fear, miss the recovery and then chase the stock out of fear of missing out.
